newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Jordan discuss changes to trade pact.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Jordan discuss changes to trade pact.

text.p: Israeli and Jordanian officials are discussing changes in their bilateral trade agreement that went into effect last April, the Israeli Industry and Trade Ministry said on Monday.
The talks are taking place in advance of a meeting scheduled for Wednesday between Israeli Industry and Trade Minister Natan Sharansky and Jordanian Trade and Industry Minister Ali Abu al-Ragheb.
The Jordanians are seeking changes in the way discounts on customs rates are calculated, to add new product categories not covered by the original agreement and to lower duties on selected goods.

The two sides are also discussing ways of easing trans-shipment of goods over their joint border. Last month, Finance Minister Dan Meridor said he would propose allowing trucks from the two countries to cross the border.

In a related development, the Israel Manufacturers Association said on Monday that a survey it conducted found that most Israeli industrialists supported a free-trade area (FTA) agreement with Jordan but would want it to be implemented gradually.

The survey of 61 executives, representing Israel's largest exporters, found 65 percent supported an FTA with Jordan, with only 25 percent opposed. However, 54 percent said Israeli customs barriers should be lowered gradually.
The association said 43 percent expressed an interest in investing in Jordan or forming alliances with Jordanian companies.

The Industry Ministry said Israeli exports to Jordan had risen from virtually nil at the start of the year to a rate of about $2.5 million a month, while imports from Jordan had reached $1.5 million a month.
